newsitem.title: UK: Supply worry, Mideast tension buoy Brent crude.
newsitem.headline: Supply worry, Mideast tension buoy Brent crude.

text.p: Early July supply worries, the disappearing June overhang and Middle East tension gave cash crude and wet Brent markets upward impetus on Tuesday, traders said.
With IPE futures up 40 cents by 1200 gmt on short covering, and a late wet market rally on Monday, inter-month spreads and short-term swaps both firmed.
Physical markets were also talked stronger, as traders pondered the effect of maintenance problems at the North Sea's Scott and Nelson fields on the delayed Forties loading programme for July.

A European major bought a Brent cargo loading 26-28 June at August Brent -60 cents, slightly less than the August -55 paid by a French major for 1 million barrels on Monday, reflecting the Tuesday purchase's promptness, the buyer said.
Some of the morning's strength stemmed from continued uncertainty over when Iraq will begin crude exports under the second term of the oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.

Iraqi annoyance over problems with the aid distribution programme was reported to be holding up the signing of contracts with crude lifters, with some pessimists not seeing Kirkuk barrels before August.

News that Iran had successfully tested an air-launched anti-ship missile last month and Washington had warned the Islamic republic against any attempt to halt shipping in the Persian Gulf also worried markets, traders said.
"That story was spooking a few people this morning," said one. "And we saw quite a lot of end-user buying last week after low numbers took out some of the June overhang."
Maintenance problems at Scott and Nelson have already knocked cargoes out of the June Forties schedule and some of the higher bidding was in anticipation that July's schedule might be
But the 22.4 million barrels announced, up from a revised 16.8 million barrels in June, was broadly in line with expectations, although the schedule was thin in the opening days of the month.
"I was expecting 23.4 million barrels had we not had the disruptions so this number is actually quite good," said one trader. "We might see some of the steam come out of the market now this is out."
July/August inter-month spreads firmed 8-9 cents to trade at -20 cents on the bullish sentiment and August/September moved at -14 cents.
CFDs also improved with the 30-04 week and July 7-11 both trading at August Brent -33 cents.
